correctness.rationale: The two central-edge orientations contribute (1+z)^2[(1+z)^b+z-1] and the swapped expression. With u=1+z and d=b-2, the residual factor is F_b(u)=2u^b+(u-2)(1+u^d); F_b(0)≠0 and F'_b(1)=b+4, giving the stipulated multiplicities. Comparing u^b to u^d and (2-u)(1+u^d) to 2u^d settles signs on (0,1) and (1,2); u≥2 is positive. For even b the negative-u polynomial has a single sign change, including b=2, and its sign at t=-u=1 is negative. For odd b the roots must be in 1<t<ρ, where H_d(t)=t^d(-2t²+t+2)-(t+2) increases with d. Independently recomputed the d=11 certificate: the coefficients through degree four of -H_11(1+x) are 2,-7,-20,22,275 and all higher ones are positive; its quartic on [0,1/4] has Bernstein coefficients 2,25/16,11/12,19/128,107/256, and at 1/4 its value, first and second derivatives are positive with second derivative increasing thereafter. The exact d=13 value at t=6/5 is 6829302128/30517578125>0. With negative endpoint signs and the two-sign-change bound, this gives exactly two simple zeros above the odd threshold. Pointwise eventual positivity inside (1,ρ) forces the two t-roots to the interval endpoints; z=-1-t reverses their order. Degree b+2 then gives real-rootedness only at b=2. value.rationale: The family gives a simple branching-tree boundary case for sink-polynomial real-rootedness outside the known claw-free scope. The result is not just a small-parameter list: it fixes both parities for every b, exhibits a finite creation threshold with simple roots, and determines limiting positions. The threshold requires genuinely more than obtaining the polynomial or bounding its possible real zeros.
